name: Menopause Physiology, Climacteric Manifestations and Hormone Replacement Therapy

reference.source: Gynaecology by Ten Teachers 21st Edition / IMS Recommendations on HRT
clinicalPearls: Menopause is diagnosed retrospectively after twelve consecutive months of amenorrhoea without pathological cause
Marked elevation of serum FSH above thirty to forty IU per liter with low estradiol reflects primordial follicle depletion
Women with an intact uterus receiving estrogen therapy must receive concurrent progestogen to prevent endometrial hyperplasia
Transdermal 17-beta estradiol avoids first-pass hepatic metabolism and does not increase venous thromboembolism risk
Topical vaginal estrogen effectively relieves genitourinary syndrome of menopause without requiring systemic progestogen
reference.pathophysiology: Ovarian senescence depletes the primordial follicle reserve below a critical threshold of approximately 1,000 follicles. Granulosa cell production of inhibin B and 17-beta estradiol ceases, removing negative feedback inhibition on the anterior pituitary and resulting in compensatory hypergonadotropic hypogonadism. Estrogen deficiency destabilizes the hypothalamic thermoregulatory center and accelerates osteoclastic bone resorption.
additionalDifferentials: Hyperthyroidism presenting with heat intolerance and palpitations
additionalInvestigations: Clinical diagnosis; serum FSH and estradiol if age under 45 or atypical presentation
Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA scan) for bone mineral density
Lipid panel and cardiovascular risk assessment
